business_problem: Vodafone wanted to use generative AI to speed up how its teams design, test, and improve TOBi conversational journeys because manual journey testing and gap analysis slowed releases and limited how much optimization the customer-service organization could do.
solution_summary: Vodafone worked with IBM to build a generative-AI testing and analysis layer around its TOBi virtual assistant. After workshops identified five candidate use cases, the team prioritized journey testing and gap analysis, then completed a five-week build with IBM Client Engineering and IBM Consulting. IBM Cloud Code Engine was used to orchestrate a service that ran multiple test scenarios in Voice Flow, while IBM watsonx.ai simulated customer interactions, analyzed the resulting transcripts, and produced sentiment, emotional, and comparative journey insights. The workflow helped Vodafone compare content between its Central Library and local market journeys and identify where conversations could be improved before deployment. TOBi itself continues to run on IBM watsonx Assistant across roughly 14 languages, and the new AI-assisted test stack shortens validation cycles while improving the quality of journey content before live customer traffic sees it.
